purpose: Accelerate preparation and source verification; preserve acceptance criteria and functional coverage.

limits: One serial and one parallel measurement on the same host; not a statistical benchmark.
System caches and other workspace activity were not controlled.
ScanCode measured the first 60 of 144 unique pinned notice texts; not the entire 200-repository audit.
No additional functional repository integrations or vulnerabilities are established by these measurements.

validation.migration_test_on_full_product: 8 passed, 1 error: unreviewed root file; the failing case was reproduced on unchanged base ae02690. The historical verifier does not accept the expanded product tree.

test_scope.git_checkout_controls: Real local Git repositories; dirty tracked bytes, dirty index, wrong HEAD, missing checkout, deterministic output and argument limits.
test_scope.tree_inventory_controls: Real Git trees; catalog/setup metadata fixtures. Native comparison separately covered all 153 trees.
test_scope.scancode_contract_controls: Simulated producer for failure/lifecycle checks; separate native benchmark used the official pinned ScanCode release.
test_scope.download_cache: Local controlled byte producers; cache hit, corruption, truncation, symlinks, interruption and concurrent publication. No remote-download latency claimed.

native_scancode_provenance: The original checkout advanced from ae02690 to 710a330 during the baseline. Imported scan code, notice code, corpus, safe_io and the used sha/copy_release functions were rechecked byte-identical to ae02690. Changes in product_review were in unused ProductIndex/CLI paths. During the optimized ScanCode run only an unused product_sources.py changed. Checkout and tree benchmarks had stable code hashes.
